title: Generative AI at Work, revised November 2024
claim: 5,172 support agents. AI assistance increased issues resolved per hour by 15% on average in this setting.
limitation: Task-level evidence in one setting, not a forecast for all firms or proof of retained profit.

title: METR experienced developer randomized trial
claim: 16 developers and 246 tasks took 19% longer with early-2025 AI tools.
limitation: Historical tools and selected experienced developers. Read S18 before using this as a current capability assessment.

title: Sanofi artificial intelligence in R&D
claim: Describes target identification, active learning for molecule design and integration of clinical and molecular data.
limitation: Dated deployment description. Does not demonstrate improved Phase II or Phase III success.

title: RELX 2025 annual report: market segments
claim: Printed page 27 describes Protégé, authoritative content, citation validation and a multi-model approach.
limitation: Product and adoption claims are management-reported. They do not isolate incremental AI profit.

title: Thomson Reuters AI for professionals
claim: CoCounsel combines professional content with workflow tools. FAQ says customer content and prompts are not used to train or improve its AI products or underlying models.
limitation: Commercial description and selected customer examples. Do not assume pooled customer-data training rights.

title: Wolters Kluwer tax and accounting solutions
claim: Offers AI-powered tax, audit, workflow and firm-management tools.
limitation: Product availability supports a use-case lead, not incremental group-level financial returns.

title: Intuit Assist
claim: Describes a generative AI financial assistant integrated with Intuit products.
limitation: No independently verified contribution margin or causal retention uplift established here.

title: SAP Joule and Business AI
claim: Describes agents operating with business context, integrations and tenant-level data isolation.
limitation: Customer data access is not equivalent to ownership or cross-customer training permission.

title: JPMorganChase 2025 COO shareholder letter
claim: Describes deployed AI in credit, fraud, personalization and employee workflows, with capacity reinvested in growth.
limitation: Management claims do not supply a controlled bank-wide AI profit bridge.

title: Visa Protect
claim: Offers AI-supported authentication, authorization and payment-fraud decision services.
limitation: Product availability alone does not establish net fraud reduction or network shareholder capture.

title: Walmart technology and agentic commerce
claim: Describes deployed shopping, support, merchant and supply-chain applications.
limitation: Broad management descriptions. Do not extrapolate selected workflow claims to total retail margins.

title: Ericsson telecom AI
claim: Explains AI for network automation, operations and network performance.
limitation: Supplier capability evidence, not demonstrated economics for Deutsche Telekom or Singtel.

title: CBRE data and technology
claim: Describes data and technology across real-estate services.
limitation: Use as a research lead for property workflows. No attributable AI profit established.

title: NAIC artificial intelligence in insurance
claim: Describes insurance uses in underwriting, pricing, claims and fraud and highlights oversight obligations.
limitation: Industry evidence cannot verify any named insurer. Survey use-or-plan-to-use figures are not adoption rates.

title: EIOPA opinion on AI governance and risk management
claim: Sets out a risk-based and proportionate approach to AI governance in insurance.
limitation: An opinion is not a substitute for checking applicable jurisdictional requirements.

title: Synopsys AI solutions
claim: Describes AI capabilities for engineering and chip design.
limitation: Specific customer improvements need design constraints and validation costs. Not direct evidence for other industrial companies.

title: IEA Energy and AI: energy optimization and innovation
claim: Distinguishes AI applications in energy operations from electricity demand for AI infrastructure.
limitation: Technical potential and scenarios are not realized returns for individual companies.

title: METR update to developer productivity experiment
claim: Follow-up explains selection and measurement problems when evaluating newer AI tools.
limitation: Do not treat the historical slowdown as a current universal effect, or newer biased samples as a precise universal speedup.

title: MSCI Global Industry Classification Standard
claim: Provides the broad 11-sector reference used as a coverage checklist.
limitation: This repository uses its own research areas and does not claim official GICS classifications for companies.

title: Siemens introduces AI agents for industrial automation
claim: Describes available engineering and operations copilots, customer implementations and an agent architecture.
limitation: The headline productivity ambition is a target. Pilot maintenance results are not group-level margin evidence.

title: Amazon million robots and DeepFleet model
claim: Describes an AI model for coordinating robot travel within Amazon fulfillment operations.
limitation: Operational claims do not isolate return on total robotics investment or consolidated AI profit.

title: CrowdStrike Charlotte AI
claim: Offers an AI analyst for security investigation and response workflows.
limitation: Vendor claims require independent detection-quality and cost evaluation.
